description: Re-tune the n=2048/4096 cooperative-cluster panel knobs (K, cb, mhyb, threads) on the current de-facto best. A sibling confirmed the cluster is the keeper for n=2048 B=8 and n=4096 B=2 (beats single-CTA 1.15x/1.71x) AND that its current K=8(n2048)/K=16(n4096), cb, and mhyb were swept on an OLDER/slower panel base, never re-measured on the faster current base (19ebe6249, which has the barrier-shortened panel + n=352/n=1024 wins). The cluster panel_factor_cluster_kernel is 61-67% of these shapes' time — its biggest cost. Re-sweep on the current base: K (n2048: 4/6/8/12; n4096: 12/14/16=hw-cap), cb (12/16/20/24), mhyb (128/256/384/512), threads (256/512), to find the now-optimal config. Use the contention-immune nsys per-solve-batch time (raw benchmark sign-flips under fleet contention). FP32 panel, TF32 trailing (loose budget safe). Keep n<=1024 + tiny-n as parent. No 'stream' substring; all guards CLEAN.

Trial 1: re-sweep n=2048 cluster knobs on the CURRENT base (parametrized K/cb/mhyb/threads into per-shape dicts). CONTENTION-IMMUNE nsys per-solve-batch (reproduced brief-40's metric: parent n=2048 K8/cb16/mhyb256/thr256=13611us, my refactor=13611us identical). SWEEPS at n=2048 B=8: K{4,6,8,12}->{15819,14788,13611,14576} (K=8 optimum, parent value confirmed); cb{12,16,20}->{15710,13611,14199} (cb=16 optimum, panel serial work ~cb^2); mhyb{128,256,384,512,768,896,1024}->{13755,13611,13512,13379,13226,13325,13476} -> mhyb=768 is the NEW optimum (2.8% under parent); K=12 at mhyb768=13934 (K=8 still best). WIN: n=2048 mhyb 256->768 routes shorter panels (m<768) to the faster single-CTA panel_factor (cluster.sync overhead doesn't pay below m=768 at B=8); cluster handles only m>=768. Also templated panel_factor_cluster_kernel on launch-bound (<256,4> byte-identical to original; adds <512,2>) to enable threads=512 sweep. n=2048 final=13312us (templated thr256). 22 tests + offgrid/invariance/diff_correctness guards ALL CLEAN. n=4096 still parent. Benchmark geomean 12139us (parent 12150us; n=2048/4096 are 2/12 shapes so geomean ~flat; raw per-shape n2048=47324us/n4096=101641us contention-inflated, hence nsys authoritative).

Trial 2: extend the re-sweep to n=4096 + finalize. CONTENTION-IMMUNE nsys per-solve-batch min-of-3. n=4096 B=2 mhyb{256,512,768,1024}->{28549,28254,28155,28191} -> mhyb=768 optimum (same lever as n=2048: route m<768 panels to single-CTA); K{12,14,16}->{28825,30103,28155} (K=16=hw-cap optimum at B=2, more CTAs fill more SMs); cb{12,16}->{31720,28155} (cb=16 optimum, cb=12 doubles trailing-GEMM count). threads=512 sweep (templated <512,2>): n=2048 thr512=13906>thr256=13312, n=4096 thr512=31289>thr256=28155 -> threads=256 BEST for BOTH (the <512,2> halves min-blocks/SM occupancy and wastes threads on the m/K-row reduction). FINAL config: n=2048 K8/cb16/mhyb768/thr256, n=4096 K16/cb16/mhyb768/thr256. min-of-3: n=2048=13248us (parent 13611 = 2.7% faster), n=4096=28133us (parent 28549 = 1.5% faster). 22 tests + offgrid/invariance/diff_correctness guards ALL CLEAN (n=2048 rankdef sfr=3.47, n=4096 dense=0.571/upper=0). Benchmark geomean 12122us. The ONLY knob that moved off parent is mhyb (256->768 both shapes); K/cb/threads parent values re-confirmed optimal on the current base.

Brief 48 cluster-knob re-sweep on the CURRENT base (19ebe6249) COMPLETE. FINAL HEAD b29d7a7 captures the best config: n=2048 K8/cb16/mhyb768/thr256, n=4096 K16/cb16/mhyb768/thr256. Metric = brief-40's CONTENTION-IMMUNE nsys per-solve-batch (median-per-launch x instances / nsolve; auto-detected nsolve=2 from cluster-kernel instance count; reproduced parent exactly), min-of-3.

VERDICT (min-of-3 vs parent min-of-3, identical codegen via templated <256,4>):
  n=2048: parent(mhyb256)=13597us -> winner(mhyb768)=13248us = 2.6% faster.
  n=4096: parent(mhyb256)=28500us -> winner(mhyb768)=28133us = 1.3% faster.

THE ONE KNOB THAT MOVED: mhyb 256->768 for BOTH shapes. Raising the cluster/single-CTA crossover routes the shorter panels (m<768) to the faster single-CTA panel_factor; the cluster's per-column cluster.sync overhead does not pay below m~768 even at B=8/B=2, so it should handle only the tallest panels. n=2048 mhyb curve {128,256,384,512,640,768,896,1024}={13755,13611,13512,13379,13300,13226,13325,13476} (clean min at 768); n=4096 {256,512,768,1024}={28549,28254,28155,28191} (flatter, min at 768).

PARENT VALUES RE-CONFIRMED OPTIMAL on the current base: K (n2048 {4,6,8,12}={15819,14788,13611,14576}->8; n4096 {12,14,16}={28825,30103,28155}->16=hw-cap, more CTAs fill more SMs at B=2); cb (n2048 {12,16,20}={15710,13611,14199}->16; n4096 {12,16}={31720,28155}->16, cb=12 doubles trailing-GEMM count); threads (templated <512,2> tested: n2048 thr512=13906>13312, n4096 thr512=31289>28155 -> 256 best BOTH; the <512,2> halves min-blocks/SM occupancy and wastes threads on the m/K-row reduction). So the stale-base concern resolved to ONLY mhyb being off; K=8/16, cb=16, thr=256 were already optimal.

22 tests + offgrid/invariance/diff_correctness guards ALL CLEAN (n=2048 rankdef sfr=3.47<<20budget, n=4096 dense=0.571/upper=0; uniform TF32 trailing safe). No 'stream' substring; +46/-20 lines vs parent. Benchmark geomean 12122us (raw per-shape useless under ~4x contention: n2048=47307us/n4096=100946us inflated 3.5x vs nsys, hence nsys authoritative).

OPEN DIRECTIONS the manager could pursue (NOT swept here, beyond this brief's K/cb/mhyb/threads grid): (1) the mhyb win means the single-CTA panel_factor (NOT the cluster) now does m=768..1792 panels at n=2048 / m=768..3840 at n=4096 -- those single-CTA panels still run threads=512 hardcoded in _blocked_qr_cluster's else-branch; a per-panel single-CTA threads/cb sweep on THAT path is untouched. (2) The cluster panel_factor_cluster_kernel itself is still 47-62% of per-solve time even at mhyb=768 (n2048 cluster=6442us of 13312; n4096 cluster=17412us of 28155) -- a STRUCTURAL cluster-kernel change (e.g. TMA panel load, tcgen05 reduction, or 2-level micro-panel inside the cluster like the single-CTA kernel has) could attack the dominant cost that no knob reached. (3) A per-panel ADAPTIVE K that grows K as panels get taller (more row-parallelism only where m is large) instead of one fixed K. (4) n=4096's trailing GEMMs are 30% of time (cutlass 128x128/128x64 tf32) -- a larger-tile or fused trailing could help that B=2 shape. (5) mhyb between 640-896 at n=4096 unrefined (curve flat ~0.1%, within noise) -- a finer min-of-5 sweep could shave a hair more.
